predecessors.name: Abbasid Caliphate
predecessors.text: Ifriqiya: 'eastern Algeria, Tunisia, and Tripolitania', territory the page calls 'not demarcated'

successors.name: Fatimid Caliphate
successors.text: Ifriqiya from Raqqada to the Zab, and Sicily

ledger.x: 800: Ibrahim I ibn al-Aghlab becomes hereditary emir of Ifriqiya.
827: the Muslim conquest of Sicily begins.
876: Ibrahim II moves the capital to Raqqada.
896: the Jebel Nafusa won back from the Rustamids.
902: Mila falls to the Fatimid movement.
902: Taormina falls and Byzantine Sicily ends.
902: Taormina, the last Byzantine stronghold, taken on 1 August; the Messina country is whole.
903: Ziyadat Allah III takes power on 27 July after Abdallah is assassinated and 'bases himself in Tunis'.
904: Setif falls to the Fatimid movement in October or November.
907: the court returns to Raqqada; 'Baghaya fell to the Kutama that year'.
907: Baghaya falls to the Kutama, the Fatimid movement.

wars.name: Revolt of the jund
wars.outcome: Crushed in 827; Mansur killed about a month after the rebels took Kairouan in September 824.

wars.name: Muslim conquest of Sicily
wars.outcome: Aghlabid victory: Palermo September 831, Messina 842/43, Enna January 859, Malta 29 August 870, Syracuse 21 May 878, Taormina 1 August 902; Sicily passes to the Fatimids in 909.

wars.name: Aghlabid-Rustamid frontier wars
wars.outcome: Siege of Tripoli 812 and the cession of Tripolitania; Ibadi tribes on the Aghlabid border rebel after 812 (undated); the Jebel Nafusa is won back in 896 (year from the Rustamid dossier).

wars.name: Aghlabid raids on southern Italy and the Emirate of Bari
wars.outcome: Taranto seized 840, Bari taken by an Aghlabid mawla about 847; Louis II's coalition takes Bari in February 871.

wars.name: Tulunid attack on the Aghlabids
wars.outcome: 'Under Ibrahim II (875-902), the dynasty faced a Tulunid attack and a Berber revolt' (Aghlabids page).

wars.name: Fatimid (Kutama) conquest of Ifriqiya
wars.outcome: The Kutama movement began in 893; Mila 902, Setif October-November 904, Baghaya 907, the battle of al-Aribus 18 March 909 and the entry into Raqqada on 25 March 909 ended the dynasty.

certainty.note: The Aghlabids page calls the territory 'not demarcated'; the Zab, Aurès and Tripolitanian frontiers with the Rustamids are tribal and move with allegiance; the Sicilian frontier moves by siege from 827 to 902 and is sharp only at the sea.
